name.evidence: PDF image 1 red case label: 'CASE NO. 272 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / SANTA GERTRUDES GRANT / THOMAS SANCHEZ COLIMA CLAIMANT'; stamped PAGE 1 (image 3) transcript title page 'for the place named "Santa Gertrudes"'. Register 'Santa Gertrudes (Colima)' agrees; Bancroft record title adds 'part and an augmentation'.

year.evidence: The ONLY Mexican concession decree in this file is dated 1846, not 1834. Stamped PAGE 11 (image 15): 'Angeles Junio 9. de 1846. Vista la peticion con que da principio este Espediente ... declaro al ciudadano Tomas Sanchez dueño en propiedad del terreno que resulta baldio entre los linderos que espresa el diseño ... Pio Pico Gobernador Constitucional de las Californias asi lo mando decretó y firmó.' The title itself, stamped PAGE 18 (image 21), closes: 'Dado en la Ciudad de los Angeles en este papel comun por falta del sellado á nueve de Junio de mil ochocientos cuarenta y seis. Pio Pico. José Mathias Moreno, Srio. Int.o' No 1834 document of any kind appears in the file.

governor.evidence: Grantor is Pío Pico, not Figueroa. Stamped PAGE 11 (image 15) and stamped PAGE 18 (image 21): 'Pio Pico Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de las Californias'; countersigned 'José Mathias Moreno, Srio. Int.o'. Figueroa's name does not appear anywhere in the pages read. The claimant's own petition, stamped PAGE 4 (image 7), attributes the underlying Santa Gertrudes rancho only to 'a grant duly made to her said husband Antonio Maria Nieto by one of the Governors of California' - it names neither a year nor a governor.

grantee.evidence: Stamped PAGE 11 (image 15) concession decree: 'declaro al ciudadano Tomas Sanchez Colima, dueño en propiedad del terreno que resulta baldio'; stamped PAGE 18 (image 21) title: 'Por cuanto el ciudadano Tomas Sanchez Colima Mejicano por nacimiento ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia la propiedad de un pedaso de terreno en aumento al que actualmente posee en el rancho de los Nietos'. Grantee and later U.S. claimant genuinely coincide here for the 1846 augmentation.

land_case.evidence: Red label image 1 'CASE NO. 272 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; every transcript leaf stamped '272 SD'; typed slip image 2 'LAND CASE 272 SD 122 pgs.'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_sd272.pdf. Board of Land Commissioners docket no. 475 (stamped PAGE 1, image 3), matching hoffman_1862 commission_no 475 / court_no 272.

outcome.evidence: Confirmed and final. Stamped PAGE 3 (image 6): 'San Francisco December 12, 1854. In the same Case Commissioner Alpheus Felch delivered the opinion of the Board confirming the claim.' The United States appealed (Attorney General notice 10 Oct 1855, stamped PAGE 111, image 124; U.S. Attorney Pacificus Ord's petition of appeal filed 5 Jan 1857, stamped PAGES 113-115, images 126-128). Appeal then abandoned: A.G. letter 20 Feb 1857, stamped PAGE 119 (image 132), 'appeal will not be prosecuted by the United States'; and the District Court order, stamped PAGE 121 (image 134), 'In the District Court of the U. States for the South. District of California. Monterey, June Term 1857. Hon Isaac S. K. Ogier Judge ... it is Ordered by the Court that the appeal in said cause be dismissed, & that the Claimant have leave to proceed upon the decree of the Commissioners heretofore rendered in his favor, as a final decree.' Filed 8 June 1857 (stamped PAGE 122, image 135).

corrections.year: 1846 per the concession decree, stamped PAGE 11 (image 15): 'Angeles Junio 9. de 1846'; title stamped PAGE 18 (image 21) 'á nueve de Junio de mil ochocientos cuarenta y seis'
corrections.governor: Pío Pico per stamped PAGE 11 (image 15) and stamped PAGE 18 (image 21): 'Pio Pico Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de las Californias'

notes:
TRANSLATION/ORIGINAL DATE CONFLICT INSIDE THE FILE: the Spanish original title (stamped PAGE 18, image 21) reads 'á nueve de Junio de mil ochocientos cuarenta y seis' and the concession decree (stamped PAGE 11, image 15) is headed 'Angeles Junio 9. de 1846'. But the Surveyor General's certified copy of the same title (stamped PAGE 12, image 16) and the sworn English translation (stamped PAGES 19-20, images 25-26) both read 'nueve de Julio' / 'the 9th of July one thousand eight hundred and forty six'. June is the sound reading: the Departmental Assembly's vacant-lands committee approved the concession on 10 June 1846 referring to 'el titulo librado a su favor con fha 9 del presente mes' (stamped PAGE 12, image 16; English at stamped PAGE 17, image 20), which a 9 July title could not precede. Witness A. F. Coronel likewise deposed 'Believe it to be the 9th of June 1846' (stamped PAGE 8, image 11), while the claim petition said 'on or about the 9th day of July 1846' (stamped PAGE 5, image 8). Year 1846 is unaffected either way.

WHY THE REGISTER'S 1834/FIGUEROA IS UNSUPPORTABLE HERE: this docket is a two-part claim - (a) a PART of Santa Gertrudes that Sánchez Colima BOUGHT, not was granted: escritura of 23 Dec 1841 by which 'Da. Maria Josefa Cota, Viuda de Antonio Maria Nieto' sold him 'un pedaso de tierra que esta al Norte de su Rancho llamado Santa Gertrudis de los Nietos' (stamped PAGE 21, images 27 AND 28), with juridical possession given 15 May 1843 by Juez 2o de Paz Antonio F. Coronel (stamped PAGES 24-26, images 31-33); and (b) the 1846 Pío Pico AUGMENTATION, which is the only concession decree in the file. So if the register's 1834/Figueroa is meant to describe the underlying Nieto-family grant, then its grantee cannot be Sánchez Colima; and if the grantee is Sánchez Colima, then the year and governor must be 1846 and Pío Pico. The register has fused the two. This is a variant of the claimant-for-grantee error: the U.S.-era claimant's name has been attached to an earlier grant's year and governor.

DUPLICATE SCAN EXPOSURE: PDF images 27 and 28 are the SAME leaf, both stamped PAGE 21 ('Testimonio a favor de D. Tomas Sanchez. Año de 1841'). Image index and stamped transcript page drift apart from that point on; by the end of the file stamped PAGE 121 = image 134 (drift 13). Cite stamped pages.

name.evidence: PDF image 1 red case label: 'CASE NO. 24 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / SANTA MANUEIA GRANT / FRANCISCO BRANCH CLAIMANT' (the gilt L is worn, reads MANUEIA for MANUELA); stamped PAGE 1 (image 4) transcript title 'for the place named "Santa Manuela"'; expediente cover stamped PAGE 7 (image 12) 'Espediente promovido por Dn. Francisco Branchi pretendiendo la posesion Juridica del paraje llamado Santa Manuela'. Hoffman's printed table misreads it 'Santa Manucla'; the register's 'Santa Manuela' is correct.

year.evidence: Concession decree, stamped PAGE 9 (image 14): 'Dado en la Ex Mision de Sta Barbara á 6 de abril de 1837. Juan B. Alvarado. Victor Prudón S.rio.' Sworn English translation, stamped PAGE 19 (image 24): 'Given at the Ex Mission of Santa Barbara this sixth of April 1837.' Departmental Deputation approved it 19 April 1837 (same leaf). The U.S. District Judge's own opinion, stamped PAGE 81 (image 87), states: 'The 1st Grant dated 6th of April 1837 was for a certain tract of land known by the name of Santa Manuela.'

governor.evidence: Stamped PAGE 8 (image 13): 'El ciudadano Juan Bautista Alvarado, Gobernador del estado y Presidente de la Excelentisima Diputación del mismo ... he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado declarandole la propiedad de él por las presentes letras'; signed 'Juan B. Alvarado' at stamped PAGE 9 (image 14). Translation at stamped PAGE 19 (image 24): 'Citizen John Bautista Alvarado Governor of the State and President of the Most Excellent Deputation of the Same.'

grantee.evidence: Stamped PAGE 8 (image 13): 'Por cuanto el ciudadano Francisco Branchi ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el terreno conocido con el nombre de Santa Manuela'; translation stamped PAGE 19 (image 24) 'Whereas Citizen Francisco Branch has for his own personal benefit and that of his Family petitioned for the land known by the name of Santa Manuela ... I have granted to him the above mentioned land'. Branch is here genuinely both the Mexican grantee and the later U.S. claimant, so this is not the claimant-for-grantee substitution.

land_case.evidence: Red label image 1 'CASE NO. 24 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; every transcript leaf stamped '24 SD'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_sd024.pdf. Board of Land Commissioners docket no. 48 (stamped PAGES 1-2, images 4 and 6), matching hoffman_1862 commission_no 48 / court_no 24.

outcome.evidence: Confirmed at every stage and final. Commission: stamped PAGE 3 (image 7), 'San Francisco Mar. 1st 1853. In Case No 48 Francisco Branch for the place named "Santa Manuela", Commissioner Hiland Hall delivered the Opinion and the Decree of Final Confirmation of this Board.' District Court affirmed: stamped PAGE 77 (image 83), 'It is ordered, adjudged and decreed that said decision of said Commissioners be hereby affirmed, And that the Appellee's Claim be deemed good and valid and Confirmed to him to the extent named in the act of Judicial Possession ... done and signed in open Court this 18 Day of March 1858. Isaac S. K. Ogier, U.S. Dist. Judge' (filed 18 March 1858, stamped PAGE 78). The Supreme Court appeal was abandoned: Attorney General's letter 18 September 1856, stamped PAGE 73 (image 79), 'confirmed to the claimant by the Commissioners, Case no. forty-eight (48), and also confirmed on appeal by the District Court, appeal in the Supreme Court will not be prosecuted by the United States', followed by the parties' stipulation filed 24 February 1857 (stamped PAGE 75, image 81) that the District Court decree 'may by order of the Court be made final'.

notes:
All six graded fields agree with the case file; Hoffman 1862 (1837 / Juan B. Alvarado / Francisco Branch / confirmed) agrees with both.

NUANCE ON GRANTEE, recorded but not graded down: the governor's concession of 6 April 1837 names Francisco Branch alone, and that is the decree the register's grantee field is graded against. But the Departmental Deputation's approving resolution of 19 April 1837, copied on the same leaf (stamped PAGE 9, image 14), reads: 'Se concedé á Dn. Franco Branchi y Manuela Carlon el sitio nombrado Sta Manuela para que lo posean en propiedad conforme a la ley de 18 de Agto de 1824 y articulo 5 del reglamento de 21 de 9bre de 1828.' So the Deputation approved the grant to Branch AND Manuela Carlón (his wife) jointly. A later phase may want to carry her as a co-grantee.

TWO GRANTS, ONE RANCHO: the file contains a second Alvarado title, stamped PAGES 17-18 (images 22-23), 'Juan B. Alvarado, Gobernador constitucional del Departamento de las Californias ... Dado en Monterey á veinte y dos de agosto de mil ochocientos cuarenta y dos', issued because the juridical possession of 23 August 1841 had run wider than the original diseño. The District Judge (stamped PAGE 81, image 87) treats both: 'The claim in this case is founded upon two different grants of the land made at different dates by Governor Alvarado to the appellee.' The register's 1837 is the original concession, which is the right one to carry; a re-reader should not mistake the 1842 regrant for a separate rancho.

SURVEY, not patent, is in the file: stamped PAGE 79 (image 85) is a Surveyor General certificate (E. F. Beale) that Rancho 'Santa Manuela' confirmed to Francisco Branch was surveyed and the plat approved 25 March 1861, with notice published 1863-1864; certified copy 2 October 1867, filed 2 November 1867. No patent copy appears, so patent_to / patent_date / glo_patent_no are left null for the GLO phase.

Confirmed by the underlying Spanish petition, stamped PAGE 43 (image 46), signed 'Angeles Febrero 22 de 1841. Pio Pico, Andres Pico.'

land_case.evidence: Red label image 1 'CASE NO. 317 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; every transcript leaf stamped '317 SD'; District Court papers headed 'Docket No. 317' (stamped PAGE 106, image 107). Board of Land Commissioners docket no. 700 (stamped PAGES 1-2, images 2-3; Secretary's certificate stamped PAGE 103, image 104), matching hoffman_1862 commission_no 700 / court_no 317. Rear binding label (image 154): 'U.S. DISTRICT COURT, Southern District of California. No. 317. THE UNITED STATES ... 317 Pio Pico, et al - Sta Margta & Las Flores. TRANSCRIPT OF THE RECORD FROM THE BOARD OF U.S. LAND COMMISSIONERS, In Case No. 700. Filed Oct 23d 1855.'

outcome.evidence: Confirmed at every level and final; NOT a case of a reversed rejection. (1) Commission Decree of Confirmation, stamped PAGES 101-102 (images 102-103): 'The claim seems to be well established and we think valid, and a decree will be entered confirming the claim. Confirmed! Filed in Office April 24, 1855' / 'In this case on hearing the proofs and allegations it is adjudged by the Commission that the claim of the petitioners is valid ... twenty square leagues ... R. Aug. Thompson, S. B. Farwell, Commissioners.' (2) The United States appealed: Attorney General Cushing's notice, Washington 3 December 1855 (stamped PAGE 104, image 105); Notice of Appeal filed 12 Feb 1856 (stamped PAGE 105, image 106); Pacificus Ord's petition for review filed 5 January 1857 (stamped PAGES 106-109, images 107-110). (3) The DISTRICT COURT affirmed: its decree of 24 October 1864 is quoted verbatim in the Supreme Court mandate, stamped PAGE 146 (image 147): 'It is ordered, adjudged, and decreed that the decision of the said board of land commissioners be, and the same is hereby affirmed, and the claim of appellees is good and valid in law, and the same is hereby confirmed to them ... A tract of land situated in the county of San Diego, containing twenty square leagues.' (4) The SUPREME COURT affirmed: mandate No. 172, December Term 1866, U.S. vs. Pio Pico, stamped PAGE 148 (image 149): 'it is now here ordered, adjudged, and decreed by this Court, that the decree of the said district Court, in this cause, be, and the same is hereby, affirmed. And it is further ordered that this cause be, and the same is hereby, remanded to the District Court of the United States for the District of California.' (5) Final decree entered: District Court order of 30 September 1874, Ogden Hoffman J., stamped PAGE 144 (image 145): 'that said Certified Copy of Mandate from the Supreme Court of the United States be filed, and that claimant have leave to proceed herein under the said decree of the said District Court affirmed as aforesaid, as under final decree.'

notes:
All six graded fields agree with the case file. Hoffman 1862 (1841 / Juan B. Alvarado / Pio Pico and Andres Pico / confirmed) agrees with both register and file.

THIS IS A LOST-GRANT CASE, and that is worth recording because it changes what 'the decree' means here. The formal titulo delivered to the Picos was destroyed: Andres Pico deposed, stamped PAGES 37-38 (images 40-41), that the grant 'was left in the Custody of said Pio Pico, where it remained until about the year 1846, when said Pio Pico left California for Sonora ... the desk in which said grant with other papers had been deposited was broken open & rifled of its contents ... at the time said Pio Pico left California in 1846, the place Santa Margarita then the stopping place of said Pio, was taken forcible possession of by a military force of the United States and given up to plunder by them on retiring ... deponent believes said grant with many other valuable papers belonging to deponent and said Pio were then destroyed.' The claim was therefore proved from the EXPEDIENTE surviving in the U.S. Surveyor General's custody, and the '"B" Translation of Grant' at stamped PAGE 39 is the sworn translation of the governor's concession decree in that expediente. That is the document the method directs grading against, and it is not testimony. Corroborating testimony (not relied on for the grades) runs the same way: Andres Pico, 'about the month of May A.D. 1841, Juan B. Alvarado, then Governor of California executed and delivered to Pio Pico and this deponent a grant in full property of the lands and Rancho claimed in this case called Santa Margarita and San Onofre' (stamped PAGE 37, image 40).

SPANISH ORIGINAL OF THE DECREE NOT READ: images 45-101 (= stamped PAGES 44-100) were not among the page images pulled, so the Spanish text of the 10 May 1841 decree inside the expediente was not seen. The date is nevertheless secure on the register's own terms: two independent exposures of the sworn translation (stamped 39 and stamped 89) both read 'Monterey May 10th 1841', the Spanish expediente cover is docketed '1841' (stamped PAGE 40), and the claimants' underlying petition is dated 'Angeles Febrero 22 de 1841' (stamped PAGE 43), which the decree must postdate. No translation/original date conflict is visible in what was read; a re-reader wanting the Spanish decree verbatim should pull images 45-101 of digicoll record 102014.

SCOPE NOTE for a later phase: the grant decree conveys 'San Onofre and Santa Margarita'. LAS FLORES was NOT granted with them; the claimants' petition states it was acquired separately, and the 1841 decree bounds the tract 'on the South by the boundaries of the Pueblo de las Flores'. The confirmed twenty square leagues nevertheless issued under the case name 'Santa Margarita y Las Flores'. The register's name field tracks the case name and is correct as such.

NO PATENT IN FILE. The last relevant leaf is the Surveyor General's certificate that the plat of survey and descriptive notes had been forwarded to the Commissioner of the General Land Office, filed 21 March 1879 (stamped PAGE 143, image 144). patent_to / patent_date / glo_patent_no left null for the GLO phase; note the register carries glo_patent_no 505 with patent_to and patent_date blank.

name.evidence: Printed transcript title page, stamped PAGE 68 (image 79): 'Transcript of the Proceedings in Case No 328, United States District Court, Southern Dist. Califor.a, John P. Davidson et al Claimant vs The United States Defendant, for the place named "Santa Paula y Saticoy"'; Commission transcript title, stamped PAGE 70 (image 81), 'Transcript of the Proceedings in case No 550 ... for the place named Santa Paula y Saticoy'. Register 'Santa Paula Y Saticoy' agrees. Bancroft record title adds the alias '(also called "Potrero de Santa Paula")'.

year.evidence: The concession decree is dated 1840, not 1843. Spanish expediente, stamped PAGE 18 (image 23): 'Monterrey abril 28 de 1840. Vista la peticion con que da principio este Espediente, la constancia que acredita en el espediente abandonado el parage que se habia concedido á Don Joaquin Ortega del Potrero de Sta Paula ... declaró á Don Manuel Jimeno Casarin dueño en propiedad del susodicho parage de Saticuy hasta los cerritos del Potrero y Sta Paula, hasta el Arroyo de Mupu y la Sierra: las lomerias de Santa Paula y las Positas ... El Sor. D. Juan B. Alvarado, Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de las Californias asi lo mando decretó y firmó de q. doy fée. Alvarado. Manuel Jimeno, Srio.' The titulo itself closes, stamped PAGE 23 (image 28): 'Dado en Monterrey á veinte y ocho de Abril de mil ochocientos cuarenta'; sworn English translation, stamped PAGE 33 (image 39): 'Given at Monterey 28 April 1840. Juan B Alvarado. Francisco Casimiro Arce, Chief Clerk.' The governor's own order issuing the testimonio, stamped PAGE 19 (image 24), refers back to 'el terreno de Saticuy y Santa Paula que obtuvo en veinte y ocho de Abril del presente año' (Monterrey, 1o de Junio de 1840), after Departmental Junta approval of 26 May 1840. The Commission's own decree of confirmation, stamped PAGE 66 (image 76), likewise dates the grant to April 1840. The register's 1843 is the date of a later CONFIRMATORY approval, not of the grant (see notes).

governor.evidence: The granting governor is Juan B. Alvarado, not Micheltorena. Stamped PAGE 18 (image 23): 'El Sor. D. Juan B. Alvarado, Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de las Californias asi lo mando decretó y firmó'; titulo heading, stamped PAGE 22 (image 27): 'Juan B. Alvarado, Gobernador constitucional del Departamento de las Californias ... he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado con sus aguas y maderas, declarandole la propiedad de él por las presentes letras'; sworn translation, stamped PAGE 32 (image 38): 'Juan B Alvarado Constitutional Governor of the Department of the Californias ... I have granted him the said tract of Land with its waters and woods, declaring him to be the Owner of the same by these present writings.' Micheltorena's 1843 paper is by its own words an approval of a grant already made, not a grant (see notes and corrections).

grantee.evidence: Manuel Jimeno Casarín, named in both instruments. Concession decree, stamped PAGE 18 (image 23): 'declaró á Don Manuel Jimeno Casarin dueño en propiedad del susodicho parage de Saticuy'; titulo, stamped PAGE 22 (image 27): 'Por cuanto Don Manuel Jimeno Casarin ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el parage conocido con el nombre de Santa Paula y Saticuy'; petition signed 'Monterrey 8 de Enero de 1840. Manuel Jimeno' (stamped PAGE 17, image 22). The register correctly carries the Mexican GRANTEE and not the U.S.-era claimant: the claimants of record are John P. Davidson, James Blair, Stephen M. Tibbetts, Joseph B. Crockett and Edward D. Baker, who bought the rancho from Jimeno by deed of 11 October 1852 (stamped PAGES 53-61, images 63-71).

land_case.evidence: Every transcript leaf stamped '328 SD'; District Court papers headed 'Docket No. 328 / Transcript No. 550' (stamped PAGES 90, 104, 106, images 101, 106, 108); PDF filename cubanc_lcf_sd328.pdf. Board of Land Commissioners docket no. 550 (Secretary Fisher's certificate under seal, stamped PAGE 67, image 77: 'in Case No. 550 on the Docket of the said Board, wherein John P. Davison, et al, are the Claimants ... for the place known by the name of "Santa Paula y Saticoy"', 8 November 1855). Matches hoffman_1862 commission_no 550 / court_no 328. Two clerical slips inside the file are worth flagging but do not affect the grade: the transcript index at stamped PAGE 72 (image 83) says 'Case No 554 was submitted on briefs', and Fisher certified one exhibit as filed 'in Case No. 527' (stamped PAGE 62, image 72) - 527 is the companion Salsipuedes/Pajaro case, because the 1852 deed conveyed both ranchos and was cross-filed.

outcome.evidence: Confirmed, and final by dismissal of the government's appeal. (1) Commission: 'San Francisco May 22d 1855. In the same Case Commissioner R. Aug.t Thompson delivered the Opinion of the Board Confirming the Claim' (stamped PAGE 72, image 83); the opinion itself ends 'R. Aug. Thompson, S. B. Farwell. Filed in Office May 22d 1855. Recorded in Record of decisions Vol 3d page 42' (stamped PAGE 66, image 76). (2) United States appealed: Attorney General Caleb Cushing's notice, Washington 31 Dec 1855, 'the appeal in the district court of the United States for the Southern district of California will be prosecuted by the United States' (stamped PAGE 88, image 100); Pacificus Ord's petition for review (stamped PAGES 90-92, images 101-104); summons issued 31 January 1857 (stamped PAGE 94, image 106). (3) APPEAL ABANDONED AND DISMISSED: Attorney General's letter, 'California Land Claims. Attorney Generals Office 12 Feb. 1857. Sir, In the case of the claim of John P. Davison, et al: confirmed to the claimant by the Commissioners, Case no. Five Hundred and fifty, (550), appeal will not be prosecuted by the United States' (stamped PAGE 96, image 108); and the District Court's order, stamped PAGE 98 (image 110): 'In the District Court of the United States for the Southern District of California. December term 1857. John P. Davison, et al. v. The United States. No. 328. Trans. No. 550. On motion of P. Ord U. States Attorney for the Southern District of California, and a suggestion to the Court that it is not the intention of the United States, to prosecute further the appeal in this cause, it is Ordered that the appeal in this cause be dismissed.' (4) Everything after 1857 in this file concerns the SURVEY only, and repeatedly recites the confirmation as already final: the District Court order of 18 April 1861 speaks of 'the survey of the land claimed in this case made under final decree' (stamped PAGE 104, image 106), and the decree of 11 August 1864, Fletcher M. Haight D.J., holds the resurvey 'in accordance with the Grant, decrees, and final decree of Confirmation' (stamped PAGE 165, image 177).

corrections.year: 1840 per the concession decree, stamped PAGE 18 (image 23): 'Monterrey abril 28 de 1840'; titulo stamped PAGE 23 (image 28) 'á veinte y ocho de Abril de mil ochocientos cuarenta'; sworn translation stamped PAGE 33 (image 39) 'Given at Monterey 28 April 1840'
corrections.governor: Juan B. Alvarado per stamped PAGES 18 and 22 (images 23 and 27): 'El Sor. D. Juan B. Alvarado, Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de las Californias asi lo mando decretó y firmó'

notes:
THE REGISTER HAS RECORDED THE CONFIRMATORY APPROVAL INSTEAD OF THE GRANT, AND HOFFMAN 1862 MADE THE SAME SUBSTITUTION. The file contains two Mexican instruments and they are not interchangeable.

(a) THE GRANT. Alvarado, Monterey, 28 April 1840, to Manuel Jimeno Casarín, of Santa Paula y Saticoy - quoted in the year/governor evidence above. It arose from a denouncement: José Joaquín Ortega's Potrero de Santa Paula, granted by FIGUEROA at 'Monterey the third [day] of July 1834' (Figueroa titulo at stamped PAGES 29-31, images 34-36, recorded 'Monterey August 1. 1834. Zamorano'), was surrendered, and Alvarado annulled it, stamped PAGE 21 (image 26): 'Monterrey 1o de Marzo de 1840. Queda sin efecto este titulo por haber declarado espontaneamente D.n Joaquin Ortega no necesitar el terreno a que se refiere y cede su derecho al mismo tiempo á Don Manuel Jimeno Casarin.' Ortega's own letter of cession, San Diego 7 June 1839, is at stamped PAGE 29 (image 34).

(b) THE 1843 PAPER, which is what the register's year and governor actually describe. Spanish at stamped PAGE 50 (image 57), sworn translation at stamped PAGE 51 (image 59), both docketed 'Doc. H.H. No. 2 annexed to the Deposition of José M.a Covarrubias': 'Citizen Manuel Micheltorena ... Whereas Don Manuel Jimeno Casarin has manifested that the Ranchos WHICH HAD BEEN GRANTED TO HIM, the first one by the name of "El Pajaro" or "Salsipuedes" and the second one called "Santa Paula" y Saticoy, are embraced within the ten littoral leagues expressed by the Law of Colonization, and that by reason thereof the said Don Manuel Jimeno now prays the approval which the Government should give in conformity with said laws; and being invested with Supreme powers conferred upon me by Order of 11th of February 1841, I HAVE APPROVED SAID GRANT, under the extent shown in the respective Sketches; that the grantee & his heirs may enjoy them as a property legally acquired and with the approval of the Supreme Government. City of Los Angeles April 1st 1843. Manl Michelta. Franco. Arce Chief Clerk.' It is an approval of an existing grant, required because the rancho lay inside the ten littoral leagues, and it covers TWO ranchos at once - so it cannot be the concession of this one.

THREE INDEPENDENT PARTIES IN THE FILE READ IT THE SAME WAY. R. C. Hopkins, Keeper of the Archives of the Land Commission and the former Mexican Government, deposed 8 June 1864, stamped PAGE 153 (image 165): 'I produce from the Archives (Mexican) an order made by Gov Micheltorena on the 1st day of April 1843, CONFIRMING THE TITLE WHICH HAD BEEN PREVIOUSLY MADE to Manuel Jimeno for the Rancho of "Santa Paula y Saticoy"', and at stamped PAGE 155 (image 167) he describes 'the Espediente of the Grant - which document Comes down to the year 1840'. The claimants' own brief on the survey, stamped PAGE 167 (image 179): 'In this Case there was a grant of one league to Ortega who surrendered it up, and Manuel Jimeno applied and obtained the Grant ... Three years after the grant was made in 1843, Micheltorena Confirmed the grant to the extension mentioned in the map.' And the 1852 deed of sale, stamped PAGE 57 (image 67): 'the Same tract of Land granted to the said Jimeno party of the first part by Juan B Alvarado heretofore Governor of California under the Republic of Mexico, by a Concesion or decree made at Monterey April 28th 1840 and by a Concesion or decree made at Monterey June 10. 1840 ... which grant was subsequently confirmed and ratified to the said Manuel Jimeno party of the first by Manuel Micheltorena Governor of California under the Mexican Republic, by an order or decree made at the City of Los Angeles April 1. 1843.'

HOFFMAN AGREES WITH THE REGISTER AND BOTH ARE WRONG AGAINST THE FILE. hoffman_1862 prints 1843 / Manuel Micheltorena, and the register prints 1843 / Micheltorena; the concession decree in the case file says 28 April 1840 / Juan B. Alvarado. This record is therefore NOT a case where the printed table and the register independently corroborate each other - they share one error, which is why the unflagged stratum cannot be assumed clean.

WHY THIS MATTERED IN THE LITIGATION, for a re-reader: the whole 1861-1864 survey fight turned on exactly this distinction. The claimants argued (stamped PAGES 167-169, images 179-181) that 'If the grant of 1840 was limited to four leagues, the subsequent Confirmation of Micheltorena in 1843, removed that limitation, and gave all the land embraced by the Map', while the United States insisted the confirmed quantity was four square leagues and excepted to a resurvey that returned eleven (District Attorney B. C. Whiting's exceptions, stamped PAGE 160, image 173). The register's collapse of the two documents into one erases the distinction the court spent three years on.

DIVERGENT INTERNAL DATE, minor: the claimants' Commission petition, stamped PAGE 73 (image 84), says the grant issued 'on the 28th of April 1840', agreeing with the decree; but the Commission's own opinion, stamped PAGE 66 (image 76), reads 'On the 2_th of April 1840' with the second digit unclear (0 or 8). The decree, the titulo, the sworn translation and the governor's June 1840 order all say the 28th, so 28 April 1840 is the reading to carry. The year is unaffected either way.

NO PATENT IN FILE. The last acts are survey acts: Surveyor General E. F. Beale approved the official survey 25 Feb 1861; exceptions; resurvey approved 8 April 1864; pro forma decree affirming it 11 Aug 1864 with leave to the United States to appeal; and the transcript index entry 'Appeal to Circuit Court 143'. patent_to / patent_date / glo_patent_no left null for the GLO phase. The register's patent_to 'John P. Davidson' is at least consistent with the claimant of record here.

THIS VOLUME IS BOUND OUT OF ORDER AND CARRIES A THIRD FOLIATION. The District Court's own index, stamped PAGE 69 (image 80), refers to a PENCIL folio sequence running to 143 ('Dismissal of Appeal by Atty Genl 85 / Order of do 87 ... Decree do do 141, 142 / Appeal to Circuit Court 143'), and that sequence does NOT track the stamped Bancroft numbers: pencil 79-80 (Petition for Review) sits at stamped 171-172, the very last leaves of the volume, while pencil 141-142 sits at stamped 164-165. Do not infer a missing second volume from that mismatch, as I nearly did: every indexed item I chased was present, just bound elsewhere - the 'Dismissal of Appeal by Atty Genl' (pencil 85) is at stamped PAGE 96 and its order (pencil 87) at stamped PAGE 98. Stamped-to-image drift also grows through the file, from 4 at the start (image 5 = stamped 1) to 13 at the end (image 185 = stamped 172), because of blank versos. Cite stamped pages.

UNREAD: stamped 44-49, 62-65, 77-87, and the odd-numbered leaves between stamped 88 and 110, plus stamped 111-147. Those are Spanish/English juridical possession detail (Nov 1847, Pablo de la Guerra), deed recording certificates, and the 1861-1863 survey papers. Nothing in them can move year/governor/grantee, which rest on the expediente, and the outcome chain is closed by the 1857 dismissal order.

year.evidence: Concession decree, written as a marginal decree on the petition in the Spanish expediente, stamped PAGE 16 (image 22): 'Angeles Abril 10 de 1845. Malo solicits called Santa Rita containing three square leagues more or less (a little) is ceded to him and to that effect let the respective title be given. Pio Pico.' governor.evidence: Pío Pico. The concession decree is signed 'Pico' (stamped PAGE 16, image 22) and its sworn translation renders the signature 'Pio Pico' (stamped PAGE 23, image 29). Pico's governorship is confirmed inside the same expediente by his order sending it to the Assembly, stamped PAGE 21 (image 27): 'Angeles Mayo 8 de 1846. Dado cuenta en sesion de hoy con este espedt.e à la Excma. Asamblea Departamental se mando pasar à la comision de terrenos baldios. Pio Pico # Agustin Olvera, D.S.' My own genuine signature is upon said paper as is also that of Juan Bandini. It is a genuine Official paper.' The District Court decree, stamped PAGE 68 (image 76), names 'Don Pio Pico'. Note the preceding marginal decree in the same expediente is Micheltorena's referral - 'Monterey En.o 25 de 1844. Inf.e el S.r Srio del despacho tomando previamente los necesarios. Micheltorena' (stamped PAGE 16; translation stamped PAGE 23) - so a careless reading of this file could have produced a Micheltorena error here; it did not.

grantee.evidence: José Ramón Malo, who is both the Mexican grantee and the U.S.-era claimant. Petition in the expediente signed 'Sta Barbara Enero 19 de 1844. J. R. Malo' (stamped PAGE 16, image 22); decree 'Se le concede à D.n Ramon Malo' (same leaf); expediente cover 'Espediente promovido por Don Ramon Malo' (stamped PAGE 15, image 21); Assembly committee 'la concesion hecha al Ciud.o Ramon Malo' (stamped PAGE 21, image 27). Hoffman 1862 prints the grantee as 'J. E. Malo', a misreading of J. R. Malo; the register's 'Jose Ramon Malo' is the correct form and matches the red label and the transcript title.

outcome.evidence: Confirmed at both levels and final by dismissal of the government's Supreme Court appeal. (1) Commission: 'San Francisco October 14, 1854. In the same case Commissioner R. Aug. Thompson delivered the opinion of the Board confirming the claim' (stamped PAGE 3, image 8); the U.S. summons describes it as 'the decision of the United States Commissioners of the 17th of October 1854 Confirming your Claim to the land called "Santa Rita" in Santa Barbara County' (stamped PAGE 65, image 73). (2) District Court: Pacificus Ord's Petition for Review filed 24 December 1856 (stamped PAGE 64, image 72), and the DECREE, December Term 1856, stamped PAGES 67-68 (images 75-76): 'This Cause coming on to be heard at this term of court on appeal from the decision of the Commissioners ... It is ordered adjudged and decreed that the decision of the said Commissioners be and the same is hereby affirmed. And it is further adjudged and decreed that the claim of the said Appellee above named is a good and valid and the same is hereby confirmed to the extent of three square leagues and no more. The land of which confirmation is hereby made is situated in the County of Santa Barbara and is known by the name of Santa Rita, being the same which was granted to the Appellee by Don Pio Pico on the 12th day of April 1845, and now had and occupied by him ... Isaac S. K. Ogier, U.S. Dist Judge for the S. Dist of Cal.' Endorsed 'Filed Dec 29th /56' (stamped PAGE 69, image 77). (3) Supreme Court: the United States appealed, and the appeal was dismissed - MANDATE No. 157, December Term 1863, United States vs. Malo, stamped PAGE 74 (image 82): 'in the present term of December, in the year of our Lord one thousand eight hundred and sixty three the said cause came on to be heard before the said Supreme Court, on the said transcript of the record, on the motion of Mr Attorney General Bates, and of Counsel for the Appellant, it is now here considered, ordered and decreed by this Court that this cause be and the same is hereby dismissed' (22 Jan.); 'Witness the Honorable Roger B. Taney Chief Justice of said Supreme Court, the first Monday of December in the year of our Lord one thousand eight hundred and sixty three'; filed in the District Court 18 October 1864 (stamped PAGE 75, image 83). This is NOT the reversed-rejection pattern: the Commission confirmed at first instance and every later step affirmed or dismissed.

notes:
All six graded fields agree with the case file. Hoffman 1862 (1845 / Pio Pico / 'J. E. Malo' / confirmed) agrees on year, governor and outcome; its grantee initial is a misprint for J. R. Malo, and its rancho name is printed 'Santa Eita' for Santa Rita. The register is right on both.

THREE DIFFERENT APRIL 1845 DATES APPEAR FOR THE SAME GRANT, all within 1845, so the register's year is unaffected; a re-reader should not treat them as a contradiction. (a) The governor's concession decree is dated 'Angeles Abril 10 de 1845' (stamped PAGE 16, translation stamped PAGE 23). (b) The formal titulo issued on that decree is repeatedly said to be of 12 April 1845: so the claimant's Commission petition, 'a grant made to him under the authority of the Mexican Government, Pio Pico Governor of the Department of the Californias bearing date of the 12th of April A.D. 1845' (stamped PAGE 4, image 9); so Pico's own deposition, 'a grant to Ramon Malo dated 12th April 1845' (stamped PAGE 5); and so the District Court decree (stamped PAGE 68). (c) The Departmental Assembly committee's approving dictamen of 26 May 1846 cites the title as 'librado con fha [1]o de Abril del año pp.o' (stamped PAGE 21), which the sworn translation renders as April of the past year (stamped PAGE 29); the day digit there is not clearly legible at this resolution and I do not certify it. The decree and the titulo are two instruments two days apart, which is ordinary.

DOCUMENTARY POSTURE: this is a clean archive case, not a lost-grant case. The claimant filed a certified tracing of the expediente from the U.S. Surveyor General's archives - Samuel D. King's certificate, stamped PAGES 21-22 (images 27-28), that 'the fifteen preceeding and hereunto annexed pages of tracing paper numbered from One to fifteen inclusive and each of which is verified by my initials (S.D.K.) exhibit true and accurate copies of certain documents on file and forming part of the said Archives in this Office', San Francisco 22 October 1852 - plus the original title and the original act of juridical possession (stamped PAGE 4, image 9). J. J. Warner deposed 4 September 1854 that he had examined the original expediente in the Surveyor General's office and knew the hands of 'Manuel Micheltorena, Pio Pico, Nicolas A Den, Joaquin Carrillo, Agustin Olvera & Santiago Arguello' (stamped PAGE 14, image 20).

BACKGROUND WORTH FLAGGING for the mission-secularization side of the project: the whole expediente is a dossier of eleven certificates (stamped PAGES 17-20 and 25-28, images 23-26 and 31-34) procured by Malo in March-April 1845 to prove that Santa Rita, 'perteneciente à la Mision de la Purisima', lay vacant because the mission had neither cattle nor Indians left - e.g. Nicolás A. Den, alcalde 1o, Santa Barbara 31 March 1845, and Antonio Rodríguez, 28 March 1845, 'la espresada Mision de la purisima à la vez no tiene bienes con q.e cubrir el referido parage, ni gente de la que pertenecia à su comunidad que lo pueda ocupar'. Against them stands Fr. Juan Moreno's report of 1 February 1844 (stamped PAGE 16, translation stamped PAGE 24), which opposed the grant: 'it is the only site which the Mission has for collecting their Cattle and if it be taken from it there will remain no way of sustaining them and the Aborigines proprietors will be obliged to abandon their great labors which does not to me seem just.'

NO PATENT IN FILE; the volume ends with the Supreme Court mandate filed 18 October 1864 and the notice of appearance of Charles E. Huse for the claimants, 18 October 1864 (stamped PAGES 70-71, images 78-79). patent_to / patent_date / glo_patent_no left null for the GLO phase.

outcome.evidence: ⚠ 'Confirmed' IS CORRECT, BUT ONLY BECAUSE THE DISTRICT COURT REVERSED A COMMISSION REJECTION. (1) THE COMMISSION REJECTED THE CLAIM. Vol A stamped PAGE 3 (image 8): 'San Francisco, April 25th 1854. In the same Case Commissioner Alpheus Felch delivered the opinion of the Majority of the Board REJECTING THE CLAIM. (Vide page 35 of this Transcript.) In the same Case Commissioner R. Aug. Thompson delivered his dissenting opinion: (Vide page 37 of this Transcript.)' The District Court restates the ground, vol B stamped PAGE 1077 (image 580): 'The Commissioners rejected this claim upon the ground that the grantee had not built a house on the premises until from two to four years after the date of the grant, that he never inhabited or cultivated the premises, and had thus failed to comply with the conditions of the grant.' (2) THE DISTRICT COURT REVERSED. Opinion, vol B stamped PAGES 1078-1080 (images 581-583): 'there has been sufficient testimony taken in this Court which establishes in its opinion a substantial compliance with the colonization laws ... This additional testimony establishes in the mind of this Court a substantial compliance by the grantee with the policy and objects of the Colonization laws of Mexico and that at no time did the grantee contemplate an abandonment of his claim ... and the decision of the Commissioners against the validity of this claim must therefore be reversed.' (3) THE DECREE, vol B stamped PAGES 1080-1082 (images 583-585): 'John Yountz adm.r Jose Dolores Pacheco, Appellant vs The United States, Appellee. District Court U.S. Northern Dist. Cal. This cause came on to be heard before a Stated Term of this Court on appeal from the final decision of the Commissioners ... upon the transcript of the proceedings and decision and the papers and evidence on which such decision was founded, and on additional testimony taken before this Court, and Counsel for both parties having appeared, Whereupon it is hereby ordered, adjudged, and decreed that said decision of the said Commissioners be in all things annulled and reversed. And it is hereby further ordered adjudged & decreed that the claim of appellant is valid to the land described in the boundaries mentioned in the grant ... to the extent of two square leagues (2 sitios) if no greater quantity be contained within said boundaries.' (4) IT BECAME FINAL AND WENT TO SURVEY. Vol B stamped PAGES 1050-1052 (images 553-555): 'At a Stated Term of the District Court of the United States of America, for the Northern District of California, held at the Court Room in the City of San Francisco on Wednesday the 30th day of April in the year of our Lord One thousand eight hundred and sixty two. Present: The Honorable Ogden Hoffman, District Judge. The United States v. John Yountz Administrator of Jose Dolores Pacheco dec.d. In the matter of the Survey and location of The Santa Rita Rancho. D.C. No. 155. L.C. No. 60' - approving the survey 'made by E. Dyer Deputy Surveyor in March 1862, containing (8894 4/100) Eight Thousand Eight Hundred and ninety four 4/100 acres of land, and approved by E. F. Beale United States Surveyor General for the State of California, on the 28th day of April 1862 ... marked "Approved April 30th 1862. Ogden Hoffman U.S. Dist. Judge."'; docket back 'Decree approving Survey. Filed April 30, 1862' (stamped PAGE 1054, image 557). (5) THE LAST APPEALS WERE KILLED. Intervenors' appeals were granted 15 October 1862 (stamped PAGES 1056 and 1058, images 559 and 561: 'Order granting appeal in behalf of Intervenor M. Murray' / '... J. Fallon') and then VACATED: stamped PAGE 1060 (image 563), 'Stipulation, and Decree vacating and setting aside orders granting appeals in behalf of J. Fallon & M. Murray. Filed Nov. 26th 1862.' The rival Bernal/Suñol exceptions had already been withdrawn by stipulation of 5 March 1862 (stamped PAGE 1048, image 551).

notes:
⭐ THIS IS THE TRAP RECORD OF THE CHUNK, AND IT PASSES. It is a bare 'Confirmed' that is true only because the District Court reversed a Land Commission REJECTION, in a MULTI-VOLUME case whose reversing decree sits in volume B - precisely the combination the method's traps section warns about. Both volumes were downloaded and the reversal + decree + survey + vacated appeals were all read, so the outcome is graded OK on evidence, not on the register's say-so. An agent who read only volume A would have found a rejection and no reversal, because volume A ends at stamped PAGE 500 in the middle of the 1861 boundary depositions (last leaf: deposition of Jose Fernandez for the intervenors Suñol, Bernal et al., 'Filed April 29, 1861').

WHY THE CLAIM WAS REJECTED AND THEN SAVED, for a re-reader: the Commission majority (Felch, with Thompson dissenting) held the grantee had not built a house within a year and so had broken the condition. Hoffman's court held the condition non-forfeiting and found substantial compliance from testimony taken after the appeal - Jose Maria Amador 'that the ranch has been cultivated since 1830 and in 1844 or 1845 grantee built a house on it', Robert Livermore 'that to his knowledge the ranch had been cultivated and occupied by the grantee since the year 1834' (vol B stamped PAGES 1078-1079, images 581-582), against the Commission's single witness Salvador Pacheco, whose 1853 deposition is at vol A stamped PAGE 6 (image 11).

THE ORIGINAL TITLE PAPER SURVIVED AND WAS PRODUCED. Unlike the Santa Margarita case, this claim did not rest on a traced copy alone: Thomas E. Everetts, custodian of the archives in the Surveyor General's office, deposed that the paper he brought from the office 'seems to be the original grant and is such a paper as was usually delivered to the grantee' (vol B stamped PAGE 1075, image 578), and the appellant's brief closes 'It is to be remarked that the grant proved in this case by Covarrubias, is the original belonging to the party' (vol B stamped PAGE 1071, image 574). Jose Maria Covarrubias, Secretary of the Prefecture of the First District in April 1839, verified his own signature on it before the Commission (vol A stamped PAGE 7, image 12).

DATE OF THE CONFIRMATION DECREE NOT ESTABLISHED. The reversing decree at vol B stamped PAGES 1080-1082 carries no date or filing endorsement on the leaves read (its docket back, stamped PAGE 1081, image 584, is blank but for the caption). It necessarily predates the 30 April 1862 survey decree, and the additional testimony it rests on was taken in 1861, so it falls in 1861 or early 1862; I did not find the entry that fixes the day. The register records no decree date, so nothing is graded on this.

THE VOLUMES ARE BOUND OUT OF CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER. In volume B the survey papers of 1862 (stamped 1048-1060) come BEFORE the 1861 briefs, opinion and decree (stamped 1071-1082), which are in turn followed by 1861 deposition notices (stamped 1083-1093). Do not infer sequence from stamped page order in this file.

ACREAGE DISCREPANCY FOR THE GLO PHASE: the decree approving the survey states 8,894 4/100 acres (vol B stamped PAGE 1052, image 555). The register carries patent_acres '8,894.01'.
